name: Glial Tumor of Neuroepithelial Tissue with Unknown Origin

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (2021)

criteria.description: Presence of glial tumor cells with neuroepithelial origin confirmed by histopathological examination
Immunohistochemical staining positive for glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and negative or inconclusive for lineage-specific markers
Molecular genetic testing excluding known defined glioma subtypes and absence of characteristic mutations (e.g., IDH1/2, 1p/19q codeletion)
MRI showing intra-axial brain lesion with features suggestive of glial tumor without definitive subtype characteristics

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of glial tumor cells with neuroepithelial origin plus immunohistochemical profile consistent with glial lineage and exclusion of known glioma subtypes by molecular testing
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary approach including neuropathology, radiology, and molecular genetics.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal neurological deficits corresponding to tumor location
Seizures of new onset in adult patients

common.symptomName: Progressive headache with increased intracranial pressure features
searchTerms: worsening headache with brain pressure signs
progressive head pain with pressure symptoms

common.symptomName: Cognitive impairment including memory and executive dysfunction
Nausea and vomiting related to raised intracranial pressure
searchTerms: nausea and vomiting from brain pressure
vomiting related to increased head pressure
feeling sick due to raised intracranial pressure
loss of part of the vision field
blind spots or missing areas in vision

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage
endocrine issues due to hypothalamus involvement
hormonal imbalance caused by brain tumor
fluid buildup in brain from tumor blockage
brain swelling due to blocked fluid flow
water on the brain caused by tumor
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

laboratory: CSF analysis typically non-specific; may show elevated protein
imaging: MRI with contrast showing intra-axial mass lesion with variable enhancement
Edema and mass effect on adjacent brain structures
other: Histopathology showing glial tumor cells without definitive lineage markers

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of IDH1/2 mutations in lower grade astrocytomas
Characteristic histopathological features such as fibrillary astrocytic cells
Distinctive 'fried egg' histology and branching capillaries
Rapid clinical progression and characteristic imaging features

redFlags: New onset seizures in adult without prior history
Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as papilledema
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition, 2021.
Orphanet: Glial tumor of neuroepithelial tissue with unknown origin (ORPHA:251668)
